meta.taxNote: WA-dealer sales are taxed at the dealer's city rate (DOR Q3-2026 combined rate + 0.5% motor-vehicle tax: 9.1–11.2% around Puget Sound), so a Kirkland or Puyallup dealer runs ~0.25 pt under Seattle and Burlington nearly 2 pt under; Oregon-dealer purchases owe 11.05% WA use tax at registration. Tax is applied to the vehicle price; the doc fee and licence estimate are added untaxed, which is how the written dealer sheets received so far are built. Earlier versions of this page used a flat 10.35%, which understated OTD by roughly $200–250.

Initial read-only market scan: 278 raw listings → 153 unique VINs → 112 pass the disqualifiers; 11-car shortlist ranked by value.

routes.title: Seattle / Eastside loop
routes.worth: Worth it if: always — this is the default Saturday-morning loop, and Kirkland (#5) now has a written $24,992 / $28,591 OTD sheet. Sit in the CarMax Renton Premium (#15) even if you buy elsewhere; it is the fixed-price benchmark. BMW Seattle (#3), Auto Connections Bellevue (#18) and Acura (#2) are sold and dropped from the route.

routes.title: North — Everett, Burlington
routes.worth: Worth it if Rodland's written number on #14 comes down toward the $31,100 OTD counter — it is the lowest-mile Premium in the set. ~30 min up I-5; Lee Johnson (#7/#12) is on the way back. Burlington (#21, the Aug 12 Signature find) is another ~40 min north of Everett: add it only after a clean history report and an emailed OTD. Doug's Lynnwood (#16) sold, so no Edmonds stop.

routes.title: South Sound — Kent, Puyallup, Olympia
routes.worth: Worth it if Puyallup puts #1/#6/#9 in writing (three cars, one stop). Add Olympia only if #13's $31,000 written OTD moves toward the $30,200 counter (CarMax Renton's equivalent is ~$31.9k); Auto 206 (#17) has a clean-fee $28,718.60 sheet but a 2024 accident on the Carfax, so stop there only if that rule is waived. Kent → Puyallup → Olympia is ~1 hr 15 min of driving one way.

routes.title: Portland metro — Portland, Troutdale, Hillsboro
routes.worth: Worth it only if a written OTD from #4 or #8/#20 clearly beats every WA finalist — it is ~175 road-miles / ~3 hr each way and the brief now treats Oregon as fallback. Tonkin Honda and Tonkin Gresham are the same dealer family (#4 + #19 in one visit); Royal Moore is ~20 min west in Hillsboro.

prose.shortlistIntro: Filtered from 163 merged records → 112 passed disqualifiers (0 accidents, non-fleet, no lemon/frame, ≥6 photos where known, VIN present or CL/iSeeCars-flagged, wanted trim). Ranked on deal-rating / KBB-FPP-delta → $-below-market → 1-owner → CPO → mi/$. At least 3 non-CarGurus sources enforced. All VINs = 0 open NHTSA recalls (2021/22/23 CX-5, checked 8/7/26).
prose.notableDQ: Notable disqualifications: 2021 Touring $22,900 Royal Moore (accident); 2021 Signature $24,490 Monroe (accident); 2021 GT 15k-mi $27,282 Tacoma (accident); 2022 Preferred $24,998 CarMax Beaverton (accident); 3 KBB listings with ACCIDENTS_REPORTED; 21 unwanted-trim (Select/base 2.5 S) not >$3k under year-avg.
prose.trimIntro: KBB national = kbb.com pricing pages (default zip, “typical” mileage). KBB Seattle = per-listing FPP averaged from KBB search results (mileage-adjusted, local). Δ = lowest clean listing − Seattle FPP (or national when Seattle n/a).
trimFootnotes: ¹ Seattle FPP = mean of per-listing kbbFppAmount from KBB search results (n=1–5 per cell).
² No Seattle FPP for this cell; Δ shown vs national — national is systematically ~$3–5k low (default-zip, higher-mileage assumption), so treat these as “at market,” not overpriced.
prose.noHaggleIntro: Walk-away numbers: if a dealer won't beat these for the same tier, buy the fixed-price unit.
prose.email: Hi, I'm Evan, looking at your [YEAR] Mazda CX-5 [TRIM], stock #[STOCK] / VIN [VIN]. I'm comparing several CX-5s in the Seattle area this week and narrowing to two or three. Could you email me an itemized out-the-door quote in writing: vehicle price, doc fee, sales tax, title/registration, and any dealer add-ons listed separately? I'm undecided on financing vs. outside lender, so please quote the cash OTD; we can talk financing after. Thanks. Happy to come see the car once I have the numbers.
prose.honestRead: Honest read: the proxy IP is on Akamai / Cloudflare / DataDome / PerimeterX blocklists, so 6 of 13 direct sources are unreachable. But the blocks cost almost nothing: Autotrader = KBB inventory (got it), TrueCar / Cars.com = AutoTempest feed (got it), CarFax listings = mostly CarGurus overlap. Net-new inventory from round 2 is ~22 cars (KBB-only VINs); everything else was already in round 1 under a different badge.
prose.dedupe: Dedupe: 278 raw → 153 unique VINs (VIN-matched) + 10 no-VIN orphans. 21 no-VIN records soft-matched to existing VINs by (year, ±1k mi, ±$250) and folded in as “also on” tags.
filterRules: Disqualify: any reported accident, fleet / rental prior use, lemon or frame-damage flag, fewer than 6 photos (where photo count is known), missing VIN (unless Craigslist / iSeeCars-flagged), missing price or miles.
Trim: unwanted trims (Sport, Select, base 2.5 S) dropped unless priced more than $3k under the year average.
Rank: deal rating / KBB FPP delta → $ below market → 1-owner → CPO → miles per dollar; at least 3 non-CarGurus sources and all 3 model years enforced on the shortlist.
prose.recallNote: NHTSA recalls: 0 open campaigns for MY2021–2023 CX-5 (checked 8/7/26). Verify by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls before purchase.
footnotes: Merge: 278 raw records (R1 200 + R2 78) → 153 unique VINs by exact VIN match; 21 no-VIN records soft-matched by (year, ±1k mi, ±$250); 10 no-VIN orphans retained (Craigslist / iSeeCars). Per-source primary contribution after dedupe: CarMax 68, CarGurus 41, KBB 22, Carvana 10, Cars.com 7, iSeeCars 5 orphan, Craigslist 5 orphan, TrueCar 2, CarSoup 2, AutoByTel 1.
KBB national FPP is default-zip (75201) at “typical” mileage — reads ~$3–5k below Seattle retail across the board. Use the Seattle-derived FPP column for delta math.
#6 KBB record has null kbbFpp (delta shows as −$25,198 in raw data — artifact, ignored).
CarMax pick #11: priorUse=[] (no fleet flag); CarMax history report available on the vehicle page.
iSeeCars adds no VINs and no history data — useful only as a cross-listing signal. Craigslist yielded zero private-party sellers in this range.
prose.sourcesHead: 13 sources across 2 rounds, plus daily re-check sweeps
prose.runnerUp: Runners-up, comfort-first: #12, the Mazda-CPO 2023 Preferred at Lee Johnson ($26,348, in the same written request as #7), and #13, the ventilated-seat 2022 Premium Plus in Olympia ($31,000 OTD quoted, holding at $30,200); #4, the dealer-confirmed Carbon Turbo in Portland ($26,102, quote in preparation), is the Oregon fallback (email only).
prose.bestRemaining: Best remaining, comfort-first: #5 2021 Grand Touring + GT Premium pkg at Kirkland ($25,192 list, $24,992 quoted in writing), then #12 Mazda-CPO 2023 Preferred at Lee Johnson ($26,348) and #13 ventilated-seat 2022 Premium Plus in Olympia ($27,389 list, $31,000 OTD quoted), then the CPO pair: #9 2023 Carbon at Puyallup ($27,699) and #7 2022 Carbon at Lee Johnson ($27,512). #4, the dealer-confirmed Carbon Turbo in Portland at $26,102, is the Oregon fallback (email only). See New candidates below.
prose.statusScope: maintained automatically as dealer replies and listing changes come in. Prices are listed asking prices; availability reflects the latest information we have and can lag the lot.
prose.statusFootnote: Ordered by current fit (comfort equipment, mileage, value). The full shortlist table has every column and sorts on any of them; the trim guide explains what each trim gets you.
prose.mapSummary: Every board car grouped by the lot it sits on, with its current asking price and where the conversation stands. Availability lags the lot — a car is only really there when the dealer says so in writing.
prose.guideReading: Comfort-first reading: the full-comfort cars are the luxury-feel standouts; the CPO Carbons trade some pampering for warranty peace of mind; the Preferreds are pleasant but plainer inside. Prices and availability move daily; the status board is the live view and the main report has the full data.
